Every snippet on this page compiles against the current state of `main`.
Most of it is drawn from [`examples/hello-deck.typ`](https://github.com/mcanouil/lanterne/blob/main/examples/hello-deck.typ); the section on steps is drawn from [`examples/stepped-deck.typ`](https://github.com/mcanouil/lanterne/blob/main/examples/stepped-deck.typ).
Both compile alongside the unit tests, so an example that stops building fails the suite.

::: {.callout-note}

## Source only, for now

The page shows the Typst that produces each deck, not the pages it produces.
Compiling Typst during the site render needs tooling that is not vendored into this repository yet, and an idealised picture drawn by hand would be a claim nothing checks.
Run `typst compile` on a snippet to see it.
:::

Each snippet assumes the import and show rule at the top of a deck:

```typst
#import "lanterne/lib.typ": *

#show: deck.with(slide-level: 2)
```

## A deck from headings

The default `slide-level` is 2, so a level 2 heading opens a slide and becomes its title, and a level 1 heading opens a section slide before it.
A heading deeper than the slide level is ordinary content.

```typst
= Results

== Recruitment

Two hundred and eighteen participants were enrolled between March and October.

=== Exclusions

Eleven were excluded before randomisation, so this line and the heading above it
sit on the slide the level 2 heading opened.

== Primary outcome

The difference was 4.2 points in favour of the intervention.
```

Three pages: the `Results` section slide, whose content is centred on the page, then `Recruitment`, then `Primary outcome`.

## Breaking a slide by hand

`#pagebreak()` at body level opens an untitled slide, whether or not a heading follows.

```typst
== Method

The trial was randomised, and analysis followed the pre-registered plan.

#pagebreak()

This continues the method, on a page of its own, with no title of its own.
```

## A slide written out in full

`slide` is complete in itself: what precedes it closes, and what follows it opens a slide of its own.
Its options are its own arguments.

```typst
== Discussion

The effect held across both pre-specified subgroups.

#slide(title: [Limitations], smaller: true)[
  The trial was single-centre, and follow-up stopped at twelve months, so nothing
  here speaks to durability beyond a year.
]

Content written after the explicit slide opens another slide.
```

## Setting one slide smaller

`slide-options` configures the slide a heading opened.
It goes immediately after that heading, and nowhere else: it must be a top level child of the slide, so one written inside a block or a grid cell is never found.

```typst
== Full protocol

#slide-options(smaller: true)

This slide asked to be set smaller, so its title and its body both step down one
notch of the theme's scale ratio, and a dense table fits on the page.
```

## A deck that splits on nothing

`slide-level: 0` disables heading splitting, leaving the explicit boundaries.
Every heading is then ordinary content, which is what a generated deck wants when the tool emitting it decides the breaks itself.

```typst
#show: deck.with(slide-level: 0)

= A heading that opens nothing

Both of these headings render as headings on one slide.

= So does this one

#pagebreak()

Only the page break opened a slide.
```

## Building a theme

`theme-tokens` takes named arguments and returns the canonical defaults with those overrides applied.

```typst
#show: deck.with(
  theme: theme-tokens(
    bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"),
    fg: rgb("#1c1c22"),
    font-heading: "Inter",
    size-base: 26pt,
    margin: 3cm,
  ),
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  info: (
    title: [Trial results],
    author: "Mickaël Canouil",
    date: datetime.today(),
  ),
)
```

`theme-merge` extends a complete theme, which is how one deck ships a light and a dark variant without repeating the tokens they share.

```typst
#let light = theme-tokens(
  bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"),
  fg: rgb("#1c1c22"),
  font-heading: "Inter",
)

#let dark = theme-merge(light, (
  bg: rgb("#1c1c22"),
  fg: rgb("#fbfbfd"),
))

#show: deck.with(theme: dark)
```

Tokens of your own go in `extra`, the one key whose contents are not validated.
It merges key by key, so setting one leaves the base theme's others in place.

```typst
#let base = theme-tokens(extra: (accent: rgb("#c2410c")))

#let variant = theme-merge(base, (extra: (accent-dim: rgb("#fdba74"))))
```

`variant.extra` now carries both `accent` and `accent-dim`.

## Linking to a slide

A labelled heading is a destination, so a link jumps to the slide that carries it.

```typst
== What a deck is <what-a-deck-is>

A level 2 heading opens a slide and becomes its title.

== Cross references

A labelled heading is a destination, so #link(<what-a-deck-is>)[this link] jumps
back to the slide that carries the label.
```

Typst refuses `@what-a-deck-is` on a heading that is not numbered, so write `#set heading(numbering: ...)` to reference a slide by name.

A slide's body is emitted once per step, so a label on it is dropped on every step but the one that keeps it, which is the first step where the element it marks is shown.
A reference therefore lands where that element first appears, and a slide with a single step, such as the one above, is unaffected.

## Revealing content with a pause

`#pause` is a step boundary, written as a top level child of the slide body.
It cuts the body there, and everything after it is revealed on the next step, so a slide with two pauses renders three pages.

```typst
== Revealed in turn

The first line is on screen from the start.

#pause

A pause opens a step boundary, so this line waits for the second step.

#pause

A third step reveals this line, and nothing above it moves when it appears.
```

Three pages: the first with one line, the second with two, the third with all three.

## An open ended step range

`uncover(range, body)` is hidden before its range and visible from there on.
An open ended range such as `"2-"` renders as many steps as the slide needs and no fewer: a slide with nothing else stepped still gets two steps out of it.

```typst
== An open ended uncover

#uncover("2-")[
  This region stays hidden through the first step and stays visible from the
  second step onward, however many steps the slide ends up with.
]

Ordinary content sits alongside it, visible from the start.
```

The hidden region still reserves its space, so nothing on the slide reflows when it appears.

## Dimming and focusing a region

`focus(range, body)` is dimmed outside its range, so one region is emphasised at a time and the rest stay legible.
`dim(range, body)` is the same idea in one direction: dimmed before its range, full strength from there on.

```typst
== Two regions, one in focus

#focus("1", [The first region is full strength on step one.])

#focus("2", [The second region takes its turn on step two.])
```

Typst 0.15 has no content opacity, so `dim` and `focus` dim by setting the text fill from the theme's `dim-opacity` token.
An image, an explicit fill and a stroke inside a dimmed region therefore do not dim.

## Showing content for one step only

`only(range, body)` is laid out on its range's steps and on no others: absent before the range and absent after it, reserving no space in either state.

```typst
== Shown for one step only

#only("2", [This line renders on step two alone: absent before it and absent after.])

The rest of the slide is visible on every step.
```

## A slide that counts its own steps

`context-slide(fn)` hands a slide body the resolved step index and total, calling `fn(index, total)` on every step.
A range written inside the callback cannot be counted, because what the callback returns does not exist when the step count is computed, so the slide's own `steps` option raises the count instead.

```typst
== A slide that counts its own steps

#slide-options(steps: 4)

#context-slide((index, total) => [Step #index of #total.])
```

Four pages, each reporting its own place in the four the option asked for.

## Collapsing a deck to a handout

`handout` collapses the steps a deck renders.
`true` renders each slide's final step alone; a range renders the steps it selects.

```typst
#show: deck.with(handout: true)
```

A handout of the stepped deck above renders one page per slide, each showing everything the slide's last step reveals.
